newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam dong easier after State Bank lowers floor.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam dong easier after State Bank lowers floor.

text.p: Vietnam's central bank pegged its official rate for the dong against the dollar slightly lower again on Monday, giving the local currency room to nudge down a few ticks in the interbank market, dealers said.
The central State Bank of Vietnam moved its official rate to 11,044 dong per dollar from 11,039 on Saturday.
Commercial banks may buy and sell at rates up to one percent either side of that rate, which means the new trading band has 10,934 as an upper limit and 11,154 as a lower limit for the currency.
With corporate demand for dollars strong in recent weeks, the dong has moved directly to its lower limit each time the floor is lowered.
One foreign banks was quoting the dong at 11,144/11,154 per dollar early on Monday.
Traders said that although liquidity remained fairly tight, demand had abated a little in recent days partly because the central bank has been selling dollars to soak up demand.
The central bank is believed to be engineering a very gradual depreciation of the dong to help tackle a record trade deficit.
